hallucinations.claim: Lagoa da Conceição: "<5 km from Praia dos Ingleses"
hallucinations.why: Ingleses is on the far north of the island, roughly 20+ km from Lagoa; Lagoa's nearby beaches are Mole/Joaquina (~10 min).

hallucinations.claim: "~€483 /month" as the typical one-bedroom rent in all five neighborhoods
hallucinations.why: One unsourced figure copied into every row; reference puts furnished one-bedrooms at ~R$3,500-4,800 incl. condo in Lagoa/Campeche, and the euro quote makes no sense for Brazil.

hallucinations.claim: "300–500 Mbps fibre is standard in these districts" pasted identically for every row
hallucinations.why: A blanket speed asserted as fact per neighborhood (sheet trap: internet speeds as facts); the range is plausible city-wide but not verified per district.

hallucinations.claim: Santo Antônio de Lisboa listed as meeting the beach requirement
hallucinations.why: Reference: Santo Antônio is quiet and colonial with no beach to speak of.

hallucinations.claim: "Each is within 5 km of one of the three beaches that 90 % of expats visit"
hallucinations.why: Unverifiable statistic presented as fact.

hallucinations.claim: Ingleses and Canasvieiras presented as walkable picks
hallucinations.why: Reference: the northern beach towns need a car and are Argentine-tourist hubs in summer; they fail the walkable criterion.

what_went_wrong: The gpt-oss draft merged Lagoa with Ingleses and pasted one rent and one internet figure into every row; the ministral review caught the merge, but the final answer still lists five places with identical numbers, a wrong distance and no pick. The search returned SEO expat-blog pages instead of listing data.
great_answer_would: Pick Lagoa da Conceição (walkable social hub) or Campeche (flat, beachfront, quieter) in a line each, say why Jurerê, Centro, Ingleses/Canasvieiras and Barra fall short, and give the six-month rental practicalities with R$ prices.
notes: Lagoa and Campeche are both listed, which is the only reason correct_current isn't lower. Jurerê is left out for an invented reason ('sources do not confirm'), not the real one (cost, dead off-season). Closing line is filler; the table repeats the same cells five times.

hallucinations.claim: "The rent for a furnished one-bedroom in Lagoa da Conceição ... is €483 per month [1]"
hallucinations.why: The reviewer noted [1] does not price Lagoa; the figure is generic. Reference: R$3,500-4,800 a month incl. condomínio (~$700-950), so €483 (~R$3,000) is low and unattributed to Lagoa.

what_went_wrong: Asked for reais and dollars, the answer gives euros and tells Pat to look up the exchange rate himself; the review flagged the €483 as unsupported but the merge kept it. The pick is only implied ("a top neighborhood") with no reason.
great_answer_would: Say 'Lagoa da Conceição, because it's the one walkable hub', give R$3,500-4,800/month incl. condo ≈ $700-950 at ~R$5.0-5.1/USD (rate stated), and add condomínio/IPTU/utilities and the 'mobiliado' filter in a line.
notes: Fails the explicit currency ask; the first sentence ('Choose a one-bedroom in one of Florianópolis's best neighbourhoods') is filler. No condo/IPTU, no seasonal markup.

hallucinations.claim: "Oviedo – quiet Galician/Spanish city"
hallucinations.why: Oviedo is the capital of Asturias, not Galicia.

hallucinations.claim: "Madrid – standard Castilian, schools around €200–€300/month" (and Toledo "tuition €200–€300")
hallucinations.why: Invented price; intensive group courses in Madrid typically run ~€150-300 per week, not per month.

hallucinations.claim: Madrid, Seville and Toledo listed as outside the tourist bubble / on a modest budget
hallucinations.why: Madrid is among Spain's priciest cities, Toledo is a day-trip tourist town, and Seville's Andalusian accent contradicts the clear-accent ask.

hallucinations.claim: "Mexico City – ... group classes typically inexpensive"; "Oaxaca – ... living costs significantly lower"
hallucinations.why: Vague claims with no figures; the reference also notes Oaxaca is more touristy.

what_went_wrong: Search returned a Spain-only listicle and a Marbella YouTube video, and gpt-oss restated that article's nine cities almost as they were. There are no Latin American budget picks (Bogotá, Quito, Sucre, Xela, Guanajuato) and no single pick, and it ends by offering to narrow the list down.
great_answer_would: Lead with Bogotá or Guanajuato/Querétaro plus Quito/Cuenca, Sucre and Xela, one reason each, one line on avoiding Caribbean coasts/Buenos Aires/Barcelona, and a budget line ($8-15/hr private, $150-250/week homestay).
notes: Granada and Salamanca are good picks per the sheet, and Barcelona/Marbella are correctly named as bubbles. Nine items with no verdict ignores Pat's 'say the best option' preference; the closing offer is padding.

hallucinations.claim: "San José, Costa Rica – round-trip flight $112"
hallucinations.why: An implausible winter round-trip fare from NYC with no date; the reviewer's correction (the drafter had called it 'weekly living $112') shows the figure is muddled.

hallucinations.claim: Atlanta $104, Dallas $123, Mumbai $610+, Delhi $638+, Tokyo $793+ as "round-trip" fares
hallucinations.why: Fares from an aggregator page with no dates; the reviewer noted they may be one-way. Exact fares presented as fact (sheet trap).

hallucinations.claim: Atlanta, Dallas and Tokyo offered as cheap winter destinations
hallucinations.why: US domestic cities and Tokyo are not cheap on the ground; reference winners are Mexico/Colombia/Guatemala/DR.

what_went_wrong: Search pulled generic flight-aggregator pages, and the draft simply listed fares from them. Living costs were never supplied (the question's explicit ask), and the merge kept Atlanta and Dallas as 'destinations'. The answer pushes the core work back to Pat.
great_answer_would: Recommend Mexico City/Oaxaca (~$1,200-1,600 all-in for two weeks) or Medellín (~$1,100-1,500), give Europe off-season and SE Asia totals with why Asia isn't cheaper, and add the timing rules (avoid Christmas week, book 5-8 weeks out).
notes: No totals, no pick and no reasoning; it answers 'cheap flight fares' rather than the question asked. Short, but empty.

hallucinations.claim: "The EIU does not publish a single 'overall winner' in the 2026 edition ... the top-place city is not named"
hallucinations.why: Wrong central fact: EIU 2026 ranks Copenhagen 1st (98/100, second year running), then Vienna, Melbourne, Sydney, Zurich.

hallucinations.claim: Monocle 2026 "does not list a top-ranked city, but Perth emerges as the most celebrated choice"
hallucinations.why: Monocle publishes a numbered top-20; the answer's claim of no ranking and a Perth 'standout' is unsupported.

hallucinations.claim: Numbeo high-scoring cluster includes "Delhi", "Beijing", "Rio de Janeiro", "New York"
hallucinations.why: Numbeo's quality-of-life index is a ranked list topped by smaller European cities; Delhi, Beijing and Rio sit well down it. The cluster and the 'no single rank' claim are both wrong.

what_went_wrong: Search reached an EIU-adjacent page about Tokyo but not the headline list, so the answer says no winner exists when Copenhagen is #1. Mercer isn't mentioned at all, and the Numbeo and Monocle readings are invented. The ministral review flagged the confusion, but the merge kept a wrong verdict.
great_answer_would: Give the EIU June 2026 top 10 (Copenhagen, Vienna, Melbourne, Sydney, Zurich, Geneva, Osaka, Adelaide, Vancouver, Tokyo), note Mercer's latest is 2024 (Zurich, Vienna, Geneva), say in one line what Monocle/Numbeo/InterNations measure, and add the expat-liveability and cost caveat.
notes: Tokyo 10th, Osaka 7th and 173 cities with the five categories are correct, so this isn't a 1. The U.S. News paragraph is irrelevant to a global question.

hallucinations.claim: "LATAM: ... 12 kg in Economy (or 16 kg in Premium Economy/Business)"
hallucinations.why: Reference: LATAM, like GOL and Azul, follows the ANAC 10 kg carry-on limit; 12 kg is a listed trap. It is repeated three times and used to advise packing heavier.

hallucinations.claim: Azul: "the size limit is not specified in the sources"
hallucinations.why: Azul uses the same 55 x 35 x 25 cm limit; the omission is hedged rather than invented, but the key fact is missing.

hallucinations.claim: Checked bag "R$180 on GOL, R$200 on LATAM, or R$250 on Azul"
hallucinations.why: Precise fees with no date or route, quoted from one blog table; checked-bag prices vary by route and booking time and cannot be verified as stated.

what_went_wrong: The source misled the gpt-oss draft into 12 kg for LATAM, and the ministral review corrected GOL's size but not LATAM's weight. It never says the 10 kg is weighed at the gate, gives no packed-weight target, and pads the answer with a generic packing list and a checked-bag section nobody asked for.
great_answer_would: State in two lines that all three carriers allow 10 kg and 55 x 35 x 25 cm incl. wheels plus a personal item, weighed at the gate, with the promo-fare caveat and a date; then give a compact list aimed at 7-8 kg with laundry every 5-7 days and the Brazil type-N adapter.
notes: Sizes (55x35x25, 45x35x20 personal item) and GOL/Azul 10 kg are right. The packing list is generic (jeans, dresses, umbrella, printed itinerary), it assumes a Peru/Bolivia itinerary Pat never gave, and it has a double period.
